# `Q-9-12` — Undefined Macro

> A `<cs:text>` element references a macro by name, but no
> `<cs:macro>` with that name is defined.

## What this means

CSL macros are reusable rendering rules: a
`<cs:macro name="author">` defines how authors are formatted,
and a `<cs:text macro="author">` later in the style invokes
that definition. This error fires when the referenced name
does not match any defined macro. The parser names the missing
macro and, when there is a close-spelled alternative, suggests
it as a hint.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo** — `<cs:text macro="auther">` referring to a
  macro named `author`. The parser's "did you mean" hint
  surfaces these when they are close enough.
- **A macro that was deleted** but whose references were not
  cleaned up.
- **A macro that lives in a different style** the author
  meant to copy from but did not.

## How to fix

If there is a "did you mean" hint, the spelling correction is
almost always the fix. Otherwise, define the missing macro at
the top level of the style, or change the reference to point
at a macro that does exist.

## Related

- `Q-9-13` — circular macro dependency: a related macro problem
  where macros reference each other in a loop.
- `Q-9-14` — duplicate macro definition: the reverse — the
  same name was defined more than once.
